items: `EXPLAIN` shows the chosen plan, never runs it
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes and reports real timings
Cost is the planner's opinion, time is measurement
A plan can look cheap and still be slow
Tree of nodes, children indented below parents
Most indented node runs first
Rows flow bottom-up, leaves feed parents
Top node returns the final rows

blocks.title: The Per-Loop Trap
blocks.text: `actual time` and `actual rows` are averages PER LOOP. Multiply by `loops` for the true total.

lines: EXPLAIN ANALYZE UPDATE orders SET paid=true;
ROLLBACK;  -- ANALYZE really ran the UPDATE

blocks.title: Red Flag
blocks.text: `Rows Removed by Filter: 998000` means you read a million rows to keep two thousand.

slides.page_title: Filter vs Index Cond vs Recheck Cond

blocks.title: Filter vs Index Cond
items: `Index Cond` narrows inside the index
`Filter` runs after rows are already fetched
`Recheck Cond` re-tests lossy bitmap pages

slides.page_title: Choosing a Scan: Seq, Index & Index Only

items: `BUFFERS` is the single most useful extra flag
`FORMAT JSON|YAML|TEXT` for tooling
`TIMING OFF` when per-node timing distorts a fast query
`Planning Time` vs `Execution Time` print at the end
A 3ms plan for a 2ms query: planning is the bottleneck
Seq reads every page in physical order
Cheapest per page, pure sequential IO
On a 200-row table it beats every index
A Seq Scan is not automatically a bug
Index Scan walks the index, then fetches the heap
One random heap fetch per match
Good for high selectivity and ordered output
Random IO cost grows with match count
Answers entirely from the index, heap untouched
Needs every referenced column in the index
Needs a visible-enough visibility map
`Heap Fetches: N` nonzero means stale VM
`VACUUM` drives Heap Fetches toward zero

slides.page_title: Bitmap Scans, Nested Loop & Hash Join

items: Too many rows for random fetches, too few for Seq
Heap read in physical order, not index order
`Recheck Cond` because the bitmap may go lossy
`Heap Blocks: exact=1204 lossy=8891`
Lossy = `work_mem` filled, whole page rechecked

blocks.title: BitmapAnd / BitmapOr
items: Combines several indexes for one query
Each index contributes its own bitmap
Why three single-column indexes beat one composite
TID Scan: direct ctid fetch, `WHERE ctid = '(0,1)'`
Function Scan: set-returning functions
Values Scan: literal `VALUES` lists
Result: constant-only, no table at all
CTE Scan / Subquery Scan: materialized intermediates

blocks.title: Selectivity Decides
blocks.text: The scan is not a preference, it is a consequence of how many rows survive the predicate.

items: For each outer row, probe the inner side
Cost roughly outer_rows times inner_cost
Optimal: tiny outer, indexed inner join key
Needs no memory at all

blocks.title: Anti-case
blocks.text: Nested Loop with a Seq Scan inner side and a large outer side is the classic disaster: O(N x M).

items: Inner side shows `loops=N` — real cost hides there
Parameterized inner scan uses the outer row's value
`Index Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)` is the tell
Builds a hash table from the smaller side (`Hash` node)
Streams the other side and probes it
Equality conditions only, never `<` or `>`
No non-equijoins, ever
Nearly free when both sides arrive in index order
Brutal when it must Sort a huge input first
Batches over 1 on a Hash: raise `work_mem`

slides.page_title: Join Shapes & How Cost Is Computed

items: Semi Join (EXISTS / IN) stops at first inner match
Anti Join (NOT EXISTS) emits outer rows with no match
`LEFT JOIN` forces the nullable side to be inner
That pins join direction and cuts planner options

blocks.title: Memoize
items: Caches inner results across loops
Pays when join keys repeat
Repeated probe becomes a lookup
Join order matters as much as join method
Planner reorders joins, only within its search limits
Unitless abstract number, not milliseconds
Comparable only between plans for the same query
Never compare across queries or tables
Ordinally meaningful inside one search, nothing more
`random_page_cost` 4.0 models a spinning disk
Set 1.1 on SSD/NVMe so index scans stop looking overpriced
`effective_cache_size` (4GB) allocates no memory
It only says how much table is likely already cached
Blocking nodes (Sort, Hash, aggregation) have startup cost
They consume all input before emitting one row
High total but zero startup wins under `LIMIT 10`
Cursor or LIMIT in play: planner favours lowest startup
Otherwise it picks the lowest total cost path

blocks.title: Additive Upward
blocks.text: A parent's total includes every child's cost. Read cost as a running sum up the tree.

blocks.title: Thresholds That Gate Features
items: `parallel_setup_cost` 1000 — small queries never go parallel
`parallel_tuple_cost` 0.1 per row moved to the leader
`jit_above_cost` 100000 — 20ms compile on a 5ms query

slides.page_title: Statistics: How the Planner Guesses Row Counts

items: Tune costs as a set, never one knob at a time
`random_page_cost` and `effective_cache_size` move real workloads
Everything else is a rounding error by comparison

blocks.q: Plan A costs 900, plan B costs 40. B is faster?
a_bullets: Only if both are plans for the SAME query
Cost ranks candidates, it does not predict ms

items: `ANALYZE` the command samples and writes `pg_statistic`
Read it through the `pg_stats` view
`default_statistics_target = 100`
Sample is about 300 x target = 30,000 rows
`avg_width` — average bytes per value
`most_common_freqs` pairs with the MCV list
MCV gives exact selectivity for skewed values
Histogram covers everything outside the MCV list
Each bucket holds roughly equal row counts

blocks.title: n_distinct Sign
items: Positive = a literal count
Negative = a ratio of rows
`-1` every value unique
`-0.5` each value appears twice

lines: if x in MCV: use its frequency

items: `correlation` near 1.0 or -1.0 makes index scans cheap
No stats: 0.5% fixed guess for equality
No stats: 33% fixed guess for an inequality range
Autovacuum ANALYZE at threshold 50 + 0.1 x reltuples changed
A fresh dump restore has no stats at all
A just-bulk-loaded table has none either
ANALYZE before you benchmark anything

lines: ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN c
ANALYZE t;  -- re-sample with the new target

blocks.title: The Independence Lie
blocks.text: Without extended stats the planner multiplies selectivities. `city='Paris' AND country='France'` underestimates badly.

blocks.title: Expression Predicates
items: `WHERE lower(email) = ...` has no stats of its own
Falls back to the 0.5% default guess
An expression index gets its own statistics
`Gather` collects rows from parallel workers
`Gather Merge` preserves worker sort order, `Gather` does not
`Workers Planned: 4 Workers Launched: 2` = pool ran out
Parallel Seq Scan divides pages among workers
Rows shown are per-worker; leader plus workers sum to total
Sort keys are printed under the node
`ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` uses a top-N heapsort
Top-N keeps only n rows, never sorts the full set
PG13+ HashAggregate spills: `Disk Usage: 12000kB`
Before that it simply blew past work_mem
`Incremental Sort` reuses a partial index ordering
It sorts only inside groups of the ordered prefix

blocks.title: Pruning Proof
blocks.text: `Subplans Removed: 7` under an Append is your receipt that partition pruning actually fired.

blocks.title: work_mem Multiplies
blocks.text: It is per sort or hash node PER WORKER. A 10-node parallel plan spends many times what you budgeted.

items: `Materialize` caches a subplan so an inner side rescans free
`WindowAgg` runs window functions
`Unique` does DISTINCT over sorted input
`Append` / `Merge Append` for partitions and UNION ALL
Compare `rows=` against `actual rows=` at every node
Start from the leaves, walk upward
Error compounds: 10x at a leaf becomes 1000x three joins up
The first big divergence is where the plan broke
Stale statistics — by far the most common
Check `last_analyze` and `last_autoanalyze`
Both live in `pg_stat_user_tables`
Correlated columns with no extended statistics
Joining on an expression the planner has no stats for
Data skew: one `customer_id` owns 90% of rows
The plan was costed for the average customer
Bloat makes `reltuples` and `relpages` lie about size
`VACUUM FULL` or `pg_repack` resets them

Past that many tables the planner stops searching join orders exhaustively
